reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that retail users interpret prediction market visualizations through a lens of cognitive bias rather than probabilistic logic. The confusion between price and probability arises because both are represented visually on the same axis, creating a perceptual overlay. In GSI, this manifests as a failure in Bayesian updating where the prior belief (P_p) is conflated with observed data (P_m). The GSE layer must therefore encode explicit disambiguation rules—such as labeling P_m vs P_p—to prevent erroneous inference. The ambiguity in chart interpretation stems from lack of contextual metadata (e.g., resolution rules, liquidity depth), which can be modeled as a signal-to-noise ratio in the visualization space. The failure mode occurs when users make decisions based on incomplete or mislabeled signals, leading to suboptimal outcomes. This is particularly acute in high-velocity markets where liquidity changes rapidly, making static visualizations misleading.
